items.title: Mayor Watters indicated a matter regarding a potential acquisition of
notes: land was discussed in Closed Session this evening.

Mayor Watters indicated Council is excited to announce the Township has purchased approximately 90 acres of land adjacent to the Centre Wellington Community Sportsplex in Fergus for a cost of $4.8 million.

He noted the acquisition of the property at 8055 Wellington Road 18 is a significant and welcome addition to our community and this land will serve as future parkland and facilitate the expansion of the sportsplex property, creating more space for recreation, events, and community activities.

Mayor Watters suggested the timing of this purchase is ideal, aligning with the launch of the 2024 Parks and Recreation Master Plan project, currently underway, and will outline Centre Wellington's parks and recreation needs for the next 30 years. He thanked staff and members of Council for seeing the need to expand our parkland next to a well- used integral recreational hub in our community. Event space, passive parkland space, sports fields, and courts will all be needed as our community grows.

motions.item_title: Request for Proposal #06-24: Consulting Services - Assessment of
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington award Request for Proposal #06-24 / Bissell Park - Consulting Services - Assessment of Options and Preparation of Technical Studies - Bissell Park Multi-Use Surface to ATA Architects Inc. at a contract price of $89,670.00, excluding HST. Councillor Wilton proposed the following amendment: THAT Council direct staff to cancel the current RFP due to increasing costs, scope and unknown future staffing and operating budget impacts; AND THAT staff bring a report back on the best next steps to replace the existing multi use pad with an inclusive and accessible alternative that is in keeping with the original spirit of the Jack MacDonald funding by the end of August 2024; AND THAT the budget for the new multi use pad remain within the currently approved budget of $418,000; AND THAT the location of a refrigerated ice pad in Centre Wellington be included for consideration in the current Parks and Recreation master planning process with recommendations for the best location for a refrigerated ice pad in Centre Wellington taking into account staffing and operational resources and budget including ice resurfacing equipment. The Chair ruled the proposed motion was not an amendment and Councillor Wilton withdrew. Deputy Mayor Lustgarten-Evoy re-read the original proposed motion as follows:
